rationale_b: Designates the Public Information Officers and Assistant PIOs to whom a section 6 request is addressed, needed to understand section 6.

rationale_a: Appeal procedure; unrelated to the 48-hour rule.
rationale_b: Appeal lies where no decision is received within the time specified in section 7(1), the remedy when the 48-hour limit is missed.

rationale_a: Penalises PIOs for missing time limits under section 7, cross-referring to the time limit but not stating the 48-hour rule itself.
rationale_b: Penalty on a PIO who does not furnish information within the time in section 7(1), the penalty for breaching the limit.

rationale_a: Designation of PIOs; unrelated to the 48-hour rule.
rationale_b: Proviso to section 5(2) adds five days to the section 7(1) response period when the application goes through an Assistant PIO, a qualification to the time limit.
Third-party notice and representation procedure before disclosing information relating to a third party, the companion procedure for personal information of others.

rationale_a: Entry/inspection powers that impose an assistance duty on persons handling hazardous substances, a related but different duty (cooperation with inspectors).
rationale_b: Section 10(2) obliges every person handling a hazardous substance to assist inspecting officers, on pain of penalty; a companion duty.

rationale_a: Definitions of 'hazardous substance' and 'handling', mentioning the terms but not stating the duty.
rationale_b: Defines 'handling' and 'hazardous substance', the terms needed to apply section 8.

rationale_a: General rule-making power listing hazardous-substance handling procedures as one of many possible measures; a rule-making/power provision.
rationale_b: Empowers the Central Government to lay down procedures and safeguards for handling hazardous substances (3(2)(vii)), the source of the safeguards section 8 requires.

rationale_a: Provides the appeal to the National Green Tribunal against directions issued under section 5, the companion remedy for the power asked about.
rationale_b: Provides an appeal to the National Green Tribunal against directions issued under section 5.
Board's power to impose monetary penalties for breach of the Act, which is the enforcement for breaching section 9 obligations.

rationale_a: Civil remedies for infringement; relevant once infringement is established, but does not say what is fair dealing.
rationale_b: Civil remedies for infringement; applies once infringement is established but does not say which uses are fair dealing.

rationale_a: Defines capacity to make treatment decisions, the threshold that determines when an advance directive is invoked and ceases to apply.
rationale_b: Defines capacity to make treatment decisions, which determines when a directive is invoked; background only.

rationale_a: Internal Committee's power to recommend action for false/malicious complaints, part of its role.
rationale_b: Committee action on false or malicious complaints; peripheral function.

rationale_a: Factors the Internal Committee must weigh in recommending compensation, part of its role.
rationale_b: Factors for Committee in determining compensation; detail of one function, marginal to constitution and role.

rationale_a: Appeal from the Internal Committee's recommendations, a companion procedure to its role.
rationale_b: Appeal against Internal Committee recommendations; the appeal from the body's decisions.

rationale_a: Internal Committee's duty to prepare and submit an annual report, part of its role.
rationale_b: Committee annual report duty; minor administrative function.
Aadhaar or passport identification required for applicants for registration or prior permission; part of the application procedure.
Grounds for cancellation of a registration certificate and three-year bar; qualification on continued acceptance.
Renewal of the registration certificate every five years; companion procedure to registration.
Registered persons must keep accounts of foreign contribution received and used; compliance condition.

rationale_a: Appeal procedure against confiscation/other orders; companion procedure, not the acceptance rule itself.
rationale_b: Appeal to High Court against refusal of permission or cancellation affecting associations; the appeal from the deciding authority.

rationale_a: Lists exceptions to section 3's prohibition (e.g. salary, business payments, gifts, remittances), a necessary qualification to whether contribution may be accepted.
rationale_b: Exempts certain receipts from section 3 prohibition; section 3 persons are mainly not associations, so marginal.

rationale_a: Procedure for designating an organisation as 'of a political nature', a category of association barred from accepting foreign contribution.
rationale_b: Procedure to declare an organisation of political nature (barred from receiving); marginal to associations generally.
Registered persons must use foreign contribution for its purpose with a 20 per cent administrative expense cap; condition on acceptance.
Identifies the Registrar of Indian vessels at each port of registry; the authority that registers.

rationale_a: Temporary pass in lieu of a certificate of registration, an alternative interim registration mechanism.
rationale_b: Temporary pass pending certificate; ancillary.

rationale_a: Custody and use requirements for the certificate of registration once issued, a companion to the registration procedure.
rationale_b: Custody and use of the certificate of registration; post-registration matter.

rationale_a: Rules on naming a registered vessel; tangential to the registration procedure itself.
rationale_b: Registrar may refuse registration under a duplicate or deceptive name; qualification on registration.

rationale_a: Procedure for registering alterations to a vessel or re-registering it, a companion aspect of the registration scheme.
rationale_b: Registration of alterations to an already registered vessel; post-registration matter.

rationale_a: Procedure for transferring a vessel's registration between ports, a companion aspect of the registration scheme.
rationale_b: Transfer of registration between ports; post-registration matter.

rationale_a: Restriction on re-registering a wrecked/abandoned vessel without a seaworthiness survey, a companion rule to registration.
rationale_b: Survey required before re-registration of wrecked or abandoned vessel; narrow condition (torn with 2, took lower).

rationale_a: Rule-making power specifically delegating the fee payable under sections 6(1) and 7(1) to rules, i.e. the enabling provision under which the RTI Rules, 2012 prescribe the application fee, but it does not itself state the amount.
rationale_b: Competent authority's power to make rules including the section 6(1) fee; rule-making by a different authority, gives no amount.
The power to issue directions whose exercise is appealable under section 5A; needed to know what can be appealed.

rationale_a: Companion provision in the same group of sections on consequences of breach, giving the right to compensation on rightful rescission.
rationale_b: Compensation for damage from non-fulfilment when a contract is rightfully rescinded; related topic but not the cited section 73.

rationale_a: This is section 18 itself: the promoter's liability to return the amount paid with interest, and to pay compensation, on failure to give possession.
rationale_b: The cited section: promoter's liability to return amount with interest and pay compensation on failure to give possession, plus compensation for defective title and other defaults.
Section 19(4) gives the allottee the matching right to claim refund with interest and compensation on the same failures.
Adjudicating officer adjudges compensation under section 18; the 'manner provided under this Act' that section 18 depends on.

rationale_a: Entry/inspection powers whose sub-sections make non-assistance or obstruction liable to penalty under section 14B, a companion to the Act's penalty scheme.
rationale_b: Entry and inspection powers, penalised via section 14B, not section 15.

rationale_a: Current penalty provision for contravening sections 9, 10 and 11, closely related to but narrower than the general contravention penalty asked about.
rationale_b: Sibling Environment Act penalty for contravening sections 9-11 only; torn with 2 but it is not section 15 or its general contravention penalty, so lower grade.

rationale_a: Cognizance-of-offences procedure for prosecuting contraventions of the Act, a direct companion to the penalty provision.
Restricts cross-border transfer of personal data by a Data Fiduciary, a specific companion obligation.
rationale_b: Government power to restrict cross-border transfers by fiduciaries; a restriction but not a general obligation.

rationale_a: States the lawful grounds for processing personal data, foundational but not itself a duty of the Fiduciary.
rationale_b: Processing permitted only for a lawful purpose with consent or legitimate use; the baseline condition the fiduciary must meet.

rationale_a: Duties a registered agent must follow, a direct companion to the registration requirement in section 9.
rationale_b: Duties of agents once registered under section 9; related but does not say whether or how to register (torn with 2, took lower).

rationale_a: Authority's function to register and maintain a public database of real estate agents, a direct companion to section 9's procedure.
rationale_b: Authority's functions include registering agents and keeping a public database of them; mentions but does not answer.
Appeal against the committee's recommendations within ninety days; the appeal from the inquiry outcome.
Complaint to the committee within three months (extendable), which starts the inquiry process; companion time limit.

rationale_a: Establishes the Central Authority and its mandate to regulate misleading advertisements, a foundational companion to its powers.
rationale_b: Establishes the CCPA with a mandate over misleading ads but does not say what it can do (torn with 2, took lower).

rationale_a: Describes how a misleading-advertisement complaint reaches the Central Authority, a companion procedure.
rationale_b: Where complaints about misleading ads may be sent; procedural pointer, not CCPA powers.

rationale_a: Search-and-seizure power used during CCPA's investigation into a misleading advertisement, a companion enforcement tool.
rationale_b: Search and seizure during CCPA investigations including misleading ads; investigative support (torn with 2, took lower).
Appeal to the National Commission within thirty days against CCPA orders under sections 20 and 21; the appeal from the answer.

rationale_a: Penalty for non-compliance with a Central Authority direction under sections 20/21 (including misleading-ad directions), the enforcement backstop for CCPA's power.
rationale_b: Punishment for failing to comply with CCPA directions under sections 20 and 21; penalty backing CCPA's advertisement orders.
Constitutes NALSA to perform the functions conferred on the Central Authority and sets its composition, but does not list those functions.

rationale_a: Right Act; requires the Central Authority (NALSA) to coordinate with other agencies in discharging its functions, but does not itself list the functions.
rationale_b: Requires the Central Authority to act in coordination with other agencies in discharging its functions; a partial statement of how NALSA works.

rationale_a: Right Act; sets out functions of the State Authority which implements NALSA's policy, but not NALSA's own functions.
rationale_b: Lists functions of the State Legal Services Authority, a different body, noting only that it gives effect to the Central Authority's policy and directions.

rationale_a: Bans capitation fees and screening in admission, a companion procedural safeguard for admissions including the 25% quota seats.
rationale_b: Bans capitation fee and screening at admission; applies to admissions generally, not the quota itself.

rationale_a: Local authority duty to ensure weaker-section and disadvantaged-group children are not discriminated against, a companion safeguard to the 25% admission requirement.
rationale_b: Local authority must ensure weaker section and disadvantaged children are not discriminated against; related but not the 25% rule.
Bars limitation where the loss resulted from the person's intentional or reckless act; key exception to the right to limit.
Distribution of the limitation fund among claimants subject to the limits; companion procedure.
Once a fund is constituted, claimants are barred from acting against other property and arrested vessels are released; effect of limitation.

rationale_a: Requires insurance to back maritime claims subject to the section 162 limitation, a companion safeguard.
rationale_b: Compulsory insurance equal to the limitation amounts; ancillary to, not part of, the limitation rule.

rationale_a: Establishes High Court jurisdiction over limitation-fund claims, a companion procedural rule.
rationale_b: High Court jurisdiction for oil pollution claims including a limitation fund; separate regime, procedural.

rationale_a: States the shipowner's right to limit liability for pollution damage under the Civil Liability Convention, an adjacent regime.
rationale_b: Shipowner limitation for oil pollution damage under the Civil Liability Convention, a separate regime excluded from general maritime-claims limitation.

rationale_a: Procedure to constitute a limitation fund for oil pollution liability, a companion mechanism under an adjacent regime.
rationale_b: Limitation fund for oil pollution liability; separate CLC regime.

rationale_a: Restricts enforcement of pollution claims once a limitation fund is established, a companion procedural consequence of limiting liability.
rationale_b: Effect of an oil pollution limitation fund on enforcement; separate pollution regime.

rationale_a: States the shipowner's right to limit liability for oil pollution damage, a companion regime to the general maritime-claims limitation.
rationale_b: Right to limit liability for bunker pollution by reference to Chapter II; separate pollution regime.

rationale_a: Procedure for a shipowner to apply for determination of limitation of bunker-oil-pollution liability, a companion procedure.
rationale_b: Bunker pollution shipowner may apply for determination of limitation under Chapter II; cross-reference from a separate regime.

rationale_a: Lets a claim be brought directly against the insurer, who may invoke the shipowner's limitation defence, a companion enforcement route.
rationale_b: Insurer's limitation for pollution damage claims; separate regime.

rationale_a: Requires owners/masters to conclude salvage contracts with salvors, a companion procedure to the reward regime.
rationale_b: Owner or master may conclude salvage contracts; on topic but says nothing on payment.

rationale_a: Central Government's powers/duties to facilitate salvage operations, a companion provision to the reward regime.
rationale_b: Government powers and directions in salvage operations; not about payment.
Director-General assists settlement of owner-salvor disputes; companion dispute procedure.
Salvage payment claims are extinguished unless brought within two years of completion of operations; time limit on the entitlement.

rationale_a: Savings clause excluding illegal creeping/sweeping from salvage entitlement, a marginal exception provision.
rationale_b: No salvage for property recovered by creeping or sweeping in breach of the Ports Act; an exception to entitlement.

rationale_a: Defines the scope of the product liability chapter, a foundational qualification for the core liability rule.
rationale_b: Scope clause applying the chapter to product liability claims; no liability conditions.

rationale_a: Liability of a product service provider, a companion/comparator provision in the same product-liability chapter.
rationale_b: Liability of product service providers, not manufacturers.

rationale_a: Liability of product sellers who are not manufacturers, a companion/comparator provision in the same chapter.
rationale_b: Liability of product sellers who are not manufacturers; different party.

rationale_a: Defines the scope of the product liability chapter, a foundational qualification for the core liability rule.
rationale_b: Scope clause applying the chapter to product liability claims; no liability conditions.

rationale_a: Liability of a product service provider, a companion/comparator provision in the same product-liability chapter.
rationale_b: Liability of product service providers, not manufacturers.

rationale_a: Liability of product sellers who are not manufacturers, a companion/comparator provision in the same chapter.
rationale_b: Liability of product sellers who are not manufacturers; different party.

rationale_a: Establishes the Central Consumer Protection Authority that regulates unfair trade practices; the deciding body, not the measures themselves.
rationale_b: Establishes the Central Authority to regulate unfair trade practices; institutional, does not set e-commerce measures.

rationale_a: District Collector's power to investigate unfair trade practice complaints, a companion enforcement procedure.
rationale_b: District Collector may inquire into unfair trade practices; general enforcement, not e-commerce measures.

rationale_a: Procedure for lodging complaints about unfair trade practices with authorities, a companion procedure.
rationale_b: Lets complaints about unfair trade practices be forwarded to authorities; general procedure, nothing on e-commerce.

rationale_a: Search-and-seizure powers used to investigate unfair trade practice complaints, a companion enforcement procedure.
rationale_b: Search and seizure in unfair trade practice investigations; procedural detail.

rationale_a: Manner of filing a complaint, including one alleging unfair trade practice, a companion procedure.
rationale_b: Consumer may file a complaint alleging unfair trade practice; general complaint route, not e-commerce measures.

rationale_a: District Commission's remedial orders when unfair trade practice allegations are proved, a companion remedy provision.
rationale_b: District Commission may order discontinuing an unfair trade practice; general remedy, not e-commerce measures.
Pawnee (a bailee under a pledge) may retain pledged goods for debt, interest and expenses; related retention right beside the lien sections.

rationale_a: Defines 'continuing guarantee' but does not address how or when it is revoked.
rationale_b: Defines a continuing guarantee as one extending to a series of transactions; needed to identify what can be revoked.

rationale_a: States the effect of ratification: ratifying part of a transaction ratifies the whole transaction, directly answering the 'effect' part of the intent.
rationale_b: Ratifying an unauthorised act ratifies the whole transaction of which it forms part; states an effect of ratification.

rationale_a: A pretended agent's liability to the third party if his purported employer does not ratify, the consequence when ratification is withheld.
rationale_b: Pretended agent liable if the alleged principal does not ratify; mentions ratification only as a condition of the agent's liability.

rationale_a: Clarifies that the Geneva Convention chapter does not apply where the New York Convention chapter applies, relevant to which regime governs.
rationale_b: Excludes the Geneva chapter for New York Convention awards; a scope clarification only.

rationale_a: Definitions section that defines 'person with benchmark disability' in passing, not about reservation.
rationale_b: Defines 'Government establishment' and 'person with benchmark disability', the two terms that decide who gets the reservation and where.
Legal capacity and support arrangements for persons with disabilities, the framework that limited guardianship operates within and qualifies.

rationale_a: Establishes the District Grievance Redressal Officer who hears complaints of non-distribution of entitled foodgrains or meals.
rationale_b: District Grievance Redressal Officer hears complaints about non-distribution; a general remedy, not the allowance.

rationale_a: Requires Central funding to a State to meet Chapter II obligations, including the allowance, in case of short supply from the central pool.
rationale_b: Central funds to States for short supply from the central pool; related to shortfall but not the allowance.

rationale_a: Defines the entitlement to subsidised foodgrains that, if not supplied, triggers the allowance under section 8.
rationale_b: Sets the foodgrain entitlement whose non-supply triggers the allowance, but does not mention the allowance.
Intermediary loses safe harbour if it fails to remove or disable access after notice from the appropriate Government; the takedown companion to blocking.
Prohibits chaining a person with mental illness in any form, a specific ban on one kind of physical restraint.
Appointment of the designated authority that issues and revokes contractor licences.
Grounds and procedure for revoking, suspending or amending a contractor's licence.
Appeal against orders under sections 47, 48 and 51 on contractor licences.
Sub-section (2) gives persons under sections 6 and 9 an appeal to the High Court against refusal of permission; companion remedy.

rationale_a: General punishment for contravening any FCRA provision, including the hospitality restriction.
rationale_b: Punishment for accepting foreign contribution in contravention of the Act; text addresses contributions, not hospitality specifically.

rationale_a: Savings clause carrying forward pre-2010 foreign-hospitality permissions into the new Act's section 6 regime.
rationale_b: Repeal and saving clause that continues old hospitality permissions under section 6; marginal.
Sub-section (2) provides an appeal to the High Court against a cancellation order under section 14(1).

rationale_a: Governs how the Board's proceedings and meetings are validly conducted.
rationale_b: Procedure at Board meetings; administrative.

rationale_a: Board's power to appoint its own officers and employees.
rationale_b: Board's officers and employees; administrative.
Appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against Board orders; companion.
Board's power to impose monetary penalties after inquiry and the factors it weighs.

rationale_a: Bars civil courts from matters within the Board's exclusive jurisdiction, defining the scope of its authority.
rationale_b: Bars civil courts on matters within the Board's powers; marginal.
Agreement for sale must fix the possession date and default interest rates payable by the promoter, which the refund right keys on.
Allottee's complaint to the Authority or adjudicating officer, the route to claim the refund.
Unpaid interest or compensation ordered against a promoter is recoverable as arrears of land revenue.
Adjudicating officer adjudges compensation and interest under sections 18 and 19; the deciding body.
Allottee's complaint to the Authority or adjudicating officer, the route to claim the refund.
Adjudicating officer adjudges compensation and interest under sections 18 and 19; the deciding body.
Penalty of up to five per cent of project cost for a promoter who contravenes other provisions of the Act, which covers breaching the section 13 bar.

rationale_a: States the District Commission's jurisdiction (by value and place), directly answering which forum hears the defective-goods complaint.
rationale_b: Gives the District Commission jurisdiction over complaints up to one crore rupees and says where the complaint is to be instituted.
State Commission jurisdiction for complaints between one and ten crore rupees and place of institution; needed for higher-value goods.
National Commission jurisdiction for complaints above ten crore rupees; needed for highest-value goods.
How the Internal or Local Committee inquires into the complaint and the ninety-day time limit; companion procedure.

rationale_a: Lists general employer duties including assisting a complaint under other law; on topic but does not identify the POSH complaint body.
rationale_b: Employer must display the Internal Committee order, support the inquiry and help the woman file a criminal complaint; relevant to where and how to complain.
Prosecution for the capitation fee and screening offences under section 13(2) needs prior sanction; the companion procedure for enforcing the ban.

rationale_a: Empowers the Child Rights Commissions to inquire into complaints of violations of the Act, including the section 17 punishment prohibition, a companion enforcement route.
rationale_b: Child rights commissions inquire into complaints on the right to education; a general complaint route that does not mention physical punishment.

rationale_a: Empowers the Child Rights Commissions to inquire into complaints of violations of the Act, including the section 17 punishment prohibition, a companion enforcement route.
General rule that a child cannot be denied admission once sought, the companion no-denial principle behind the age-proof-specific rule.
rationale_b: No denial of admission for late applicants; a parallel no-denial rule, but about timing, not age proof.

rationale_a: Addresses what counts as sufficient consideration for a surety's guarantee, a narrow context, not the general rule that a promise without consideration is void.
rationale_b: States what suffices as consideration for a guarantee and its illustration says a guarantee given without consideration is void; a partial, context-specific answer.
States no consideration is necessary to create an agency, a statutory instance where consideration is not required; partial answer to the exceptions.
Only a person of the age of majority and sound mind may employ an agent; a capacity rule excluding minors, but limited to agency.
A person not of the age of majority cannot become an agent responsible to his principal; partial capacity rule in agency context.

rationale_a: States that a finder of goods who takes them into custody has the same responsibility as a bailee, directly answering what duties the finder owes.
rationale_b: States a finder who takes goods into custody has the same responsibility as a bailee.

rationale_a: Requires every establishment (including private) to notify an equal opportunity policy, a companion compliance obligation to the non-discrimination-in-employment rule.
rationale_b: Every establishment must notify and register an equal opportunity policy under the employment chapter; companion obligation.

rationale_a: Sets up the grievance redressal procedure for non-compliance with the non-discrimination-in-employment section, the companion complaint mechanism.
rationale_b: Grievance Redressal Officer to receive complaints of non-compliance with section 20; the redress procedure.

rationale_a: General right against discrimination on the ground of disability, the overarching principle underlying protection from dismissal, though not employment-specific.
rationale_b: General prohibition on discrimination on ground of disability unless proportionate to a legitimate aim; applies beyond employment, not the employment rule itself.
Punishment for contravening provisions of the Act, which covers breach of the non-discrimination rule.

rationale_a: States the patient's right to confidentiality of mental health information and the health professional's duty to keep it confidential subject to listed exceptions, directly answering whether a hospital needs consent to share records.
rationale_b: States the right to confidentiality of mental health information and the exceptions permitting release without consent.
Bars release of photographs or information to the media without consent and extends confidentiality to digital records.

rationale_a: Governs the patient's right to access and any withholding of his own medical records, a closely related but distinct question from third-party disclosure of records.
rationale_b: Person's own right to access records and withholding from them; about records but not disclosure to others without consent.

rationale_a: Governs informed consent for research participation, a related but distinct consent context from sharing medical records.
rationale_b: Research on case notes of persons unable to consent is allowed if anonymity is secured; an exception to use of records without consent.

rationale_a: Right to access one's own medical records and permissible withholding of information, a closely related but distinct question from third-party disclosure without consent.
rationale_b: Person's own right to access records and withholding from them; about records but not disclosure to others without consent.

rationale_a: Governs informed consent for research participation and permits anonymised case-note study without consent, a narrower, related consent context but not general disclosure of records.
rationale_b: Research on case notes of persons unable to consent is allowed if anonymity is secured; an exception to use of records without consent.

rationale_a: Requires reporting an ill-treated or neglected person with mental illness to a Magistrate, a companion route that can lead to a Magistrate ordering admission.
rationale_b: Police report to Magistrate about neglected persons, leading to section 102; marginal.

rationale_a: Lists the nominated representative's duty to apply for the person's admission under sections 87/89/90, a companion procedural role in non-consensual admission.
rationale_b: Nominated representative's duties include applying for admission under sections 89/90; cross-reference only.

rationale_a: Gives the admitted person a right to be informed of the provision and criteria under which he was admitted, a companion safeguard to the admission process.
rationale_b: Right to information about admission criteria and review; incidental companion right.

rationale_a: Lets an aggrieved patient or representative apply to the Board for redress, the appeal mechanism against an admission decision.
rationale_b: General applications to the Board for violation of rights; not specific to challenging admission.
Appeal to the High Court against a Board decision, including on admission.

rationale_a: Defines 'independent patient' admission; contextual definition but does not itself address non-consensual admission.
rationale_b: Admissions are to be independent except where supported admission is unavoidable; frames the exception asked about.

rationale_a: Describes voluntary (independent-patient) admission, the consensual alternative whose limits define when supported admission without consent is used instead.
rationale_b: Voluntary independent admission and its capacity condition; context, not admission against will.
Allows holding an independent patient for 24 hours against a discharge request for assessment for supported admission.
Emergency treatment, including transport for assessment, without the person's consent for up to 72 hours.

rationale_a: Gives the Board power to inquire into a breach of a Data Fiduciary's obligations and impose penalty; the deciding body for the consequence.
rationale_b: Board's power to inquire into personal data breaches or breach of fiduciary obligations on complaint and impose penalty; the deciding body.
Procedure for the Board's inquiry leading to closure or penalty under section 33; companion procedure.
Appeal from Board orders to the Appellate Tribunal; the appeal route from the penalty.

rationale_a: Provides for enforcing Appellate Tribunal orders as a decree, part of the enforcement chain that follows a penalty.
rationale_b: Execution of Appellate Tribunal orders as decrees; procedural, does not state the consequence of breach.

rationale_a: Lets the Board direct mediation of a complaint, a companion procedure to the consequence pathway.
rationale_b: Board may refer a complaint to mediation; peripheral to what happens to a breaching company.

rationale_a: States that the Board may impose a monetary penalty on a person whose breach of the Act is significant, directly answering the consequence asked about.
rationale_b: Board may impose monetary penalty from the Schedule for significant breach, with factors for quantum; the direct consequence.
Right of grievance redressal against the fiduciary for non-performance of obligations or rights, to be exhausted before the Board; companion remedy.
Board inquires into complaints of breach of fiduciary obligations or the principal's rights; the body that decides if erasure is refused.

rationale_a: Exempts an intermediary from liability for third-party information it hosts, subject to due-diligence and takedown conditions, directly answering whether a website is liable for user posts.
rationale_b: Intermediary not liable for third-party information it hosts, subject to conditions and loss of immunity on actual knowledge; the answer.

rationale_a: Confirms contracts formed through electronic means are not unenforceable merely for that reason, closely tied to the validity question.
rationale_b: Contracts formed electronically are not unenforceable for that reason; related e-commerce validity rule, not signatures (lower grade chosen).

rationale_a: Gives electronic form the same legal status as writing, the companion recognition provision alongside signature recognition.
rationale_b: Legal recognition of electronic records (writing requirement); parallel rule but not about signatures (lower grade chosen).

rationale_a: Sets how a subscriber accepts a Digital Signature Certificate, a companion step in establishing a valid digital signature.
rationale_b: Acceptance of DSC and subscriber's certification; on topic but not legal validity.

rationale_a: Lists giving legal service to eligible persons as a State Authority function; cross-refers to eligibility without stating it.
rationale_b: State Authority must give legal service to persons satisfying the Act's criteria; the providing body.
Appeal where no decision is received within the section 7 time, with appeal disposal within 30/45 days; companion remedy.
Information on human rights violations from excluded security organisations must be provided within forty-five days; exception to the time limit.

rationale_a: Lists failure to respond in time as a ground for complaint to the Information Commission but does not state the time limit itself.
rationale_b: Lets the Information Commission take a complaint when no response is given within the time limit; the remedy for missing the deadline, but does not set it.
For information from excluded intelligence organisations about human rights violations, the reply is due within forty-five days, overriding section 7; a qualification to the time limit.

rationale_a: Governs making an RTI request and the 5-day transfer window between authorities, not the PIO's response deadline.
rationale_b: RTI request procedure, including the five-day limit for transferring an application to another public authority; companion to the response deadline.

rationale_a: Gives the Information Commission the duty to receive and inquire into complaints from a person refused access or not given a timely response, a complaint route alongside the section 19 appeal.
rationale_b: Complaint to the Information Commission by anyone refused access, given no response in time, or unable to file a request; a direct route besides appeal.

rationale_a: Sets penalties the Commission may impose on a defaulting PIO, a possible outcome rather than the appeal route itself.
rationale_b: Penalties the Commission imposes on a PIO who wrongly refuses or fails to reply, decided on a complaint or appeal; the consequence of the remedy.

rationale_a: Lets the Government prohibit dealing with currency received in contravention of FCRA, a consequence tied to unlawful receipt of foreign contribution.
rationale_b: Government may bar dealing with currency accepted in breach of the FCRA; enforcement on the topic that does not say whether or how NGOs may accept contributions.
Applicants for prior permission, registration or renewal may be required to give office-bearers' Aadhaar numbers; a companion requirement for getting permission.
FCRA certificates must be renewed, and are renewed for five years; a companion requirement for keeping the right to accept.

rationale_a: Requires anyone certified or given prior permission under section 12 to receive foreign contribution only through a designated FCRA bank account, part of what a registered NGO must do.
rationale_b: Certificate holders must receive foreign contribution only in an "FCRA Account" at the specified SBI branch; an operational requirement, while the registration rule itself is in unadmitted sections.

rationale_a: Empowers seizure of currency received in contravention of FCRA, a consequence tied to unlawful receipt of foreign contribution.
rationale_b: Seizure of currency received in breach of the FCRA; enforcement on the topic without stating the conditions for acceptance.

rationale_a: Bars a person twice convicted of foreign-contribution offences from accepting any foreign contribution for five years, a narrow penal consequence rather than the general registration rule.
Lists receipts (salary, ordinary business payments, gifts from relatives, etc.) that fall outside the section 3 restriction, clarifying what does not count as regulated foreign contribution.

rationale_b: Registered recipients must use the money for its stated purpose and keep administrative expenses to twenty per cent; conditions attached to accepting foreign contribution.

rationale_a: Lets the Central Government require prior permission or bar receipt of foreign contribution in specified cases, a qualification on who may accept it.
rationale_b: Government may bar a person or organisation from accepting foreign contribution or require prior permission; a qualification on who may accept.

rationale_a: Defines how a 'day' is computed for workers on shifts crossing midnight; touches shift timing but not the hour limit itself.
rationale_b: For shifts past midnight, sets how hours and the weekly holiday are counted; a companion to the hour limits.
Seafarers' right to repatriation at no cost and the owner's duty to maintain and return them; a companion entitlement after losing the ship.

rationale_a: States the ship owner must pay each seafarer onboard an indemnity against unemployment when the vessel is lost or founders, directly answering the query.
rationale_b: On loss or foundering of a vessel, the owner must pay each seafarer onboard a prescribed indemnity against unemployment; the direct answer.

rationale_a: Entitles a seafarer whose service is terminated by the wreck, loss or abandonment of the vessel to wages on prescribed terms, directly answering what a seafarer gets when the ship is lost.
rationale_b: A seafarer whose service ends because of the wreck or loss of the vessel is entitled to wages on prescribed terms; states the entitlement asked about.

rationale_a: Provides for recovery of the wages and compensation due to a seafarer who is missing or lost with the vessel, a companion rule for the case of death.

rationale_b: Relief and repatriation of abandoned seafarers, including conveying shipwrecked seafarers to port at the owner's cost; a companion entitlement.

rationale_a: Lets a judicial authority direct an insolvency-related dispute to arbitration, a related but narrow scenario distinct from an ordinary contract's arbitration clause.
rationale_b: An arbitration clause binds an insolvent's receiver, and the insolvency court may order a matter submitted to arbitration; a specific instance of court referral.

rationale_a: Requires a judicial authority to refer parties to arbitration under a valid New York Convention arbitration agreement unless it is null, void or inoperative, the same mechanism as the domestic rule but limited to foreign awards.
rationale_b: A judicial authority must refer parties to arbitration on request unless it finds the agreement prima facie null or inoperative; the referral rule, but only for New York Convention agreements.
No judicial authority may intervene in matters governed by Part I except as the Part provides; a qualification limiting court involvement where there is an arbitration agreement.
Appeal lies from an order refusing to refer parties to arbitration under section 45; the appeal from the referral decision.
Appeals before the State or National Commission should be disposed of within ninety days of admission; the companion deadline for the appeal stage.
After a mediation settlement report, the Commission must record the settlement and dispose of the complaint within seven days; a companion deadline for complaints settled by mediation.

rationale_a: Companion procedure describing who may file a complaint and how, directly tied to the act of filing a complaint.
rationale_b: How and by whom a complaint is filed with the District Commission, but sets no time limit.

rationale_a: Companion procedure on how and by whom a complaint is filed with the District Commission.
rationale_b: How and by whom a complaint is filed with the District Commission, but sets no time limit.

rationale_a: Central Authority's power to impose civil penalties (up to ten/fifty lakh rupees) on manufacturers, endorsers and publishers of false or misleading advertisements; a direct administrative-penalty answer the pool missed.
rationale_b: Central Authority may impose penalties up to ten lakh (fifty lakh for repeat) on manufacturers, endorsers and publishers of false or misleading advertisements and ban endorsers.
Punishes non-compliance with Central Authority directions under s.21 to discontinue or modify a misleading advertisement.
Companion procedure: courts take cognizance of the s.89 offence only on a complaint by the Central Authority.
Board's inquiry procedure on a breach intimation or complaint, concluding with penalty under s.33.
Appeal against Board orders, including penalty orders, to the Appellate Tribunal within sixty days.

rationale_a: Declares every agreement restraining a person from exercising a lawful profession, trade or business void, subject to the good-will exception; directly answers the intent and was missing from the pool.
rationale_b: Declares every agreement restraining anyone from a lawful profession, trade or business void to that extent, with the sale-of-goodwill exception.

rationale_a: A party who rightfully rescinds a contract is entitled to compensation for damage from non-fulfilment; a companion compensation-for-breach provision adjoining the missing stipulated-penalty section.
rationale_b: Compensation to a party rightfully rescinding a contract; on contract damages but not about a sum named in the contract.

rationale_a: Defines 'pledge', 'pawnor' and 'pawnee'; sets up but does not itself state the pawnee's rights on default.
rationale_b: Defines pledge, pawnor and pawnee; context only, states no pawnee rights on default.

rationale_a: Gives the pawnee a right of retainer over the pledged goods for the debt, interest and expenses; the pawnee's core security right, closely related to what happens when a pawnor fails to pay.
rationale_b: Pawnee may retain the pledged goods for the debt, its interest and necessary expenses until paid.
Qualifies the retainer right: pawnee may not retain for other debts absent contract, though subsequent advances are presumed covered.
Pawnee's right to recover extraordinary preservation expenses from the pawnor.
Identification of priority and Antyodaya households that determines who qualifies for the per-person entitlement.
Central allocation of foodgrains to States as per section 3 entitlements; supply-side, does not state the per-person amount.

rationale_a: States the exact entitlement: five kilograms of foodgrains per person per month for priority households, thirty-five kilograms per household per month for Antyodaya households.
rationale_b: States that each person in a priority household gets five kilograms of foodgrains per month (35 kg per AAY household) at subsidised prices under TPDS.
Food security allowance payable when entitled quantities of foodgrains are not supplied.

rationale_a: Provides free meals to malnourished children via anganwadi, a related but distinct nutritional-support entitlement, not the mid-day meal scheme itself.
rationale_b: Free meals via anganwadi for malnourished children; a companion child-nutrition entitlement but not the school mid-day meal itself.
Requires States to implement schemes covering the section 5 entitlements with Centre-State cost sharing.
Food security allowance payable when entitled meals are not supplied, a remedy for non-provision of the mid-day meal.
Requires States to implement schemes covering section 4 entitlements (including maternity benefit) with Centre-State cost sharing.
Designates the Registrar of Indian vessels, the authority that closes registration under section 43.
Provisional registration may be cancelled or deemed closed, with unsatisfied mortgages staying on the register; a related closure scenario.

rationale_a: Governs re-registration of a vessel after its registration has ceased (wrecked/abandoned), the companion rule to closure of registration.
rationale_b: Survey needed before re-registering a vessel that ceased to be registered after wreck or abandonment; adjacent to, not about, closing registration.

rationale_a: Directly provides the procedure for an owner to apply to close (deregister) an Indian vessel's registration, subject to no outstanding mortgage or wage claims.
rationale_b: Owner may apply to the Registrar to close a vessel registration if no unsatisfied mortgage or wage claims remain; Registrar closes it and records the closure.
Rule-making power including form and manner of application for closure of registration under section 43.

rationale_a: Rule-making power to set accessibility standards; enabling provision rather than the deadline itself.
rationale_b: Central Government to formulate accessibility standards rules for the physical environment and services; the deadlines run from notification of these rules.
Accessible transport facilities at bus stops, stations and airports; accessibility measures without a deadline.

rationale_a: Requires new buildings to follow accessibility rules before plan approval or occupation; addresses new construction, not a deadline for making existing buildings accessible.
rationale_b: Bars building permission and completion certificates for new buildings not adhering to accessibility rules; companion rule for new construction, no time limit for existing buildings.
Service providers must make services accessible per section 40 rules within two years of notification of those rules, extendable by the Central Government.
Accessibility standards rules covering information and communications; the standards behind accessible communication obligations.
Time limit for service providers to meet accessibility rules; on accessibility generally, not specific to deaf communication.

rationale_a: Requires treatment information be given in sign language among other means, but in the specific context of mental-healthcare consent capacity, not a general interpreter obligation.
rationale_b: Requires information on treatment decisions to be given in sign language or visual aids where needed; a specific instance of accessible communication.
Sub-section (4) requires PIOs to provide assistance enabling sensorily disabled persons to access information; an accessible-communication duty without naming sign language.

rationale_a: Conciliation process for settling a complaint, expressly excluding monetary settlement; on topic but a different, non-compensation track.
rationale_b: Conciliation where no monetary settlement may be the basis; a qualification on compensation.
Appeal within ninety days against Committee recommendations under section 13, including compensation awards.
Penalty on employer who fails to act under section 13; touches enforcement only marginally.

rationale_a: Composition and tenure of the Local Committee, the body that decides and awards compensation to the aggrieved woman.
rationale_b: Composition of the Local Committee, one of the bodies that fixes compensation; composition does not help determine the amount.
Factors the adjudicating officer weighs in fixing compensation for contraventions under the chapter that includes unauthorised access.

rationale_a: Punishes identity theft (fraudulent use of another's password/signature) under the IT Act, a related but distinct cybercrime from unauthorised access/hacking.
rationale_b: Punishes fraudulent use of another person's password or unique identification feature with up to three years and fine; closely related credential misuse but not unauthorised access as such.
Punishes unauthorised penetration or access to computer resources when done with terrorist intent or to obtain restricted data, up to life; an aggravated form of hacking only.
IT Act offences apply to acts outside India involving computers in India; a jurisdictional extension only.
Computers and accessories involved in contraventions of the IT Act are liable to confiscation; an additional consequence for hacking.

rationale_a: Punishes publishing/transmitting obscene electronic material, a companion offence to the sexually-explicit-image offence.
rationale_b: Punishes publishing or transmitting obscene material electronically; covers part of the conduct but is about obscenity generally, not private images.

rationale_a: Punishes publishing or transmitting sexually explicit material in electronic form, the core offence the query asks about.
rationale_b: Punishes publishing or transmitting sexually explicit material in electronic form, the core offence for sharing explicit images.
Punishes publishing sexually explicit material depicting children; an instance of the offence limited to child victims.
Penalty for disclosure without consent by persons who obtained material under powers conferred by the Act; privacy-related but not the general image offence.

rationale_a: Recovery/enforcement of Tribunal and Authority orders; companion enforcement machinery.
rationale_b: Recovery and enforcement of orders including the tribunal's; peripheral.

rationale_a: Qualifications for Tribunal Chairperson/Members; companion detail on the body's composition.
rationale_b: Qualifications and appointment of tribunal members; administrative detail (lower grade chosen).

rationale_a: Term of office of Tribunal Chairperson/Members; companion detail.
rationale_b: Term of office of tribunal members; administrative detail that does not help identify the forum or its jurisdiction.

rationale_a: Staffing of the Tribunal; companion administrative detail.
rationale_b: Staff of the Appellate Tribunal; peripheral.

rationale_a: Filling vacancies in the Tribunal; companion administrative detail.
rationale_b: Filling vacancies in the tribunal; peripheral.

rationale_a: Administrative powers of the Tribunal Chairperson; companion detail.
rationale_b: Administrative powers of the tribunal's Chairperson; peripheral.

rationale_a: Penalty on promoters for defying Tribunal orders; consequence of the Tribunal's role.
rationale_b: Penalty on promoters for disobeying tribunal orders; peripheral to identifying the tribunal.

rationale_a: Penalty on agents for defying Tribunal orders; a consequence of the Tribunal's role, not its constitution.
rationale_b: Penalty on agents for disobeying tribunal orders; peripheral.

rationale_a: States the ship owner's liability for pollution damage caused by the ship, the central liability rule under the Civil Liability Convention chapter.
rationale_b: Core rule making the ship owner liable for pollution damage caused by oil from the ship, with exceptions.
High Court admiralty jurisdiction over oil pollution liability claims; the forum for compensation.

rationale_a: Lets the ship owner limit liability for pollution damage; companion qualification to the liability rule.
rationale_b: Ship owner's right to limit liability for oil pollution and loss of that right for intentional or reckless conduct.

rationale_a: Lets a compensating ship owner/insurer step into the claimant's rights against the fund; companion to the core liability rule.
rationale_b: Subrogation of insurers or owners who paid pollution compensation; a technical side rule (lower grade chosen).
Consolidation and distribution of the fund among claimants and High Court order for compensation where no fund is set up.
Time limit (three and six years) for bringing oil pollution compensation claims.

rationale_a: Defines 'contributing oil', 'Fund' and 'guarantor' used in the Fund-compensation scheme; needed context.
rationale_b: Definitions for the Fund chapter; mentions oil pollution compensation fund only in passing.

rationale_a: Governs contributions funding the Compensation Fund; companion to how compensation is financed.
rationale_b: Oil importers' contributions to the international compensation Fund; background to the Fund, not victim compensation.

rationale_a: Grants seafarers paid annual leave, but under a different Act from the general labour code on the topic.
rationale_b: Ship owners must allow seafarers paid annual leave; an instance of the entitlement for a narrow class of workers with conditions left to rules (lower grade chosen).

rationale_a: High Court's power to make procedural rules for appeals under section 72; companion to the underlying appeal provision.
rationale_b: High Court may make rules for appeals made to it under section 72; cross-refers to the appeal provision and is rule-making.

rationale_a: Makes High Court orders passed in an appeal executable as a decree; companion to the underlying appeal provision.
rationale_b: Makes money orders, including those of the High Court in appeals, executable as decrees; mentions such appeals in passing.
Establishes District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions; a redressal body.
Manner of filing consumer complaints with the District Commission; a redressal procedure for consumer disputes.

rationale_a: Adjudication of penalties for ignoring the Grievance Redressal Officer's recommendation; companion enforcement step.
rationale_b: Adjudication of penalties under section 33 by a State Commission member; peripheral.

rationale_a: Designates the District Officer who administers grievance functions under the Act; the deciding body, not the procedure itself.
rationale_b: Notification of District Officers under the POSH Act; does not itself describe a redressal procedure.
Procedure for an aggrieved woman to complain of sexual harassment to the Internal or Local Committee within three months.

rationale_a: Protects a child with disability from being separated from parents on the ground of disability, a direct family-life right.
rationale_b: No child with disability to be separated from parents on ground of disability except by court order in the child's best interest.

rationale_a: Bars capitation fees and screening procedures in admission, a direct protection for children seeking admission.
rationale_b: Protects children from capitation fees and screening at admission, with fines for breach.

rationale_a: Bars denial of school admission after the extended admission period, a direct protective right of the child.
rationale_b: No child to be denied admission even after the extended admission period.

rationale_a: Grants a child a direct statutory right to transfer to another school to complete elementary education.
rationale_b: Child's right to transfer to another school with a transfer certificate that cannot delay admission.

rationale_a: Imposes the core duty on local authorities to provide free compulsory elementary education to every child and prevent discrimination against weaker-section children.

rationale_b: Special safeguards for admitting minors to mental health establishments: best interests, separate accommodation, attendant, Board review.
Punishes dealing with articles or currency in contravention of a prohibitory order served under section 10.
Sub-section (3) punishes an intermediary failing to comply with a government blocking direction; a government, not a regulatory authority or tribunal.

rationale_a: Penalises operating an unregistered establishment and non-payment of penalty; adjacent enforcement provision rather than order non-compliance itself.
rationale_b: Penalties for running an unregistered mental health establishment; not about disobeying orders.

rationale_a: Provides that a mental health establishment failing to comply with the Authority's order may have its registration cancelled, a direct consequence for disobedience.
rationale_b: Authority may cancel a mental health establishment's registration if it fails to comply with the Authority's inspection order; a sanction, not a monetary penalty.

rationale_a: Makes a port liable to penalty for failing to comply with Central Government directions on reception facilities, an instance of the rule but narrow/context-specific.
rationale_b: Ports failing to comply with Central Government directions on reception facilities are liable to an unspecified penalty; mainly about reception facilities.

rationale_a: Sets the enquiry/appeal procedure and fine for non-payment of a penalty already imposed by an officer, the companion enforcement mechanism.
rationale_b: Procedure for officers to impose penalties, with a fine for not paying an imposed penalty; only tangential to disobeying an authority's order.

rationale_a: Criminalises failing to comply with a requisition or order issued under the Code, alongside obstruction offences.
Penalises non-registration under section 3 and escalates on non-compliance with resulting orders; primarily a registration offence.
rationale_b: Sub-section (2) punishes a promoter who does not comply with orders issued for non-registration; partly on point.

rationale_a: Power of the State (not Central) Government to supersede the State Authority; same mechanism but wrong level of government for this intent.
rationale_b: Supersession power, but held by the State Government over a State Authority rather than by the Central Government.
Requires the Central Government to formulate accessibility rules; a subject-specific rule-making mandate rather than the general power.

rationale_a: Central Government's power to amend the Schedule by notification, a companion delegated legislative power to rule-making though distinct from 'rules'.
rationale_b: Power to amend the Schedule by notification; delegated power but not rule-making.
Board's inquiry procedure, ending in proceedings under section 33 on completion; the companion procedure for imposing penalties.
Appeal to the Appellate Tribunal against Board orders, including penalty orders, within sixty days.
Voluntary undertaking bars proceedings, and breach of it is dealt with under the section 33 penalty; a qualification to penalties.

rationale_a: Directs that penalty sums collected by the Board go to the Consolidated Fund of India, the companion administrative step after a penalty.
rationale_b: Penalty sums go to the Consolidated Fund of India; administrative detail only.

rationale_a: Empowers Central Government to direct blocking of public access to a repeat-offending Data Fiduciary's resource; a different consequence triggered by penalties, not the penalty provision itself.
rationale_b: Blocking of a Data Fiduciary's services after penalties in two or more instances; a follow-on consequence of penalties.

rationale_a: Central Government's power to amend the Schedule that sets penalty amounts, capped at double the original, a companion power over penalty quantum.
rationale_b: Power to amend the Schedule, capping any penalty increase at twice the original; a limit on amendment rather than a penalty provision.
Sub-section (2) allows appeal to the High Court against refusal of registration under section 12 or cancellation under section 14.

rationale_a: Criminalises seeking registration by fraud or false representation; touches registration but is an offence provision, not about the certificate process itself.
rationale_b: Punishes seeking registration or prior permission by fraud or false representation; a penalty tied to registration.
Bars parties from using conciliation views, admissions and proposals as evidence in other proceedings, a companion protection to conciliation confidentiality.

rationale_a: Central Authority's power to refer a matter for investigation, mentions receiving a 'complaint' only in passing among other triggers.
rationale_b: Central Authority's preliminary inquiry and investigation on receipt of a complaint or information.

rationale_a: States the orders/reliefs the District Commission issues once a complaint is proved, the outcome of the complaint process.
rationale_b: Orders the District Commission issues when allegations in a complaint are proved; the outcome of a complaint.

rationale_a: Governs how notice of a complaint is served on the opposite party, a companion procedural step to filing a complaint.
Bars a court from taking cognizance of an offence without a complaint by the Central Authority; a criminal-complaint trigger, a different sense of 'complaint' from the consumer dispute complaint.
rationale_b: Offences under sections 88 and 89 can be taken cognizance of only on a complaint by the Central Authority; a complaint provision in the criminal sense.
Requires States to set up an internal grievance redressal mechanism such as call centres and helplines.

rationale_a: Establishes the District Grievance Redressal Officer who hears complaints of non-distribution of entitled foodgrains, the core complaint mechanism under this Act.
rationale_b: District Grievance Redressal Officer hears complaints on non-distribution of foodgrains, with appeal to the State Commission.

rationale_a: Civil-court style inquiry powers of the State Commission and forwarding of a criminal complaint to a Magistrate, the deciding body's powers rather than the complaint provision itself.
rationale_b: State Food Commission's civil-court powers in inquiries; mentions forwarding a complaint to a Magistrate only in passing.

rationale_a: Sets the composition/membership of the Central Authority, the structural companion to the section establishing it.
rationale_b: Composition of the Central Authority; the companion to its establishment.

rationale_a: Lists the Central Authority's functions once already constituted, not how it is established.
rationale_b: Functions of the Central Authority once established; companion to its establishment provision.

rationale_a: Lists the State Authority's functions once already constituted, not how it is established.
rationale_b: Functions of the State Authority once established; companion to its establishment provision.
Requires the State Authority to constitute Mental Health Review Boards by notification; establishes an adjudicating body rather than an Authority as such.

rationale_a: Empowers the Central Government to take prescribed measures against unfair e-commerce practices, the enabling provision under which the E-Commerce Rules (and its grievance officer requirement) were made.
rationale_b: Lets the Central Government prescribe measures against unfair practices in e-commerce, the parent power for the E-Commerce Rules; it does not itself mention grievance officers (torn with 2, took the lower).

rationale_a: Ties the governing substantive law to whether the place of arbitration is in India, a direct legal consequence of the seat.
rationale_b: Applicable substantive law where the place of arbitration is in India; uses the place of arbitration as a trigger but says nothing about fixing the seat.
